messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT INC-2026-4321 created — sustained 5xx spike from Dedicated pool `dedicated-prod-eu-2` (customer-impacting). Error rate 12% over 3m, overall latency ↑ 2x. Paging primary on-call @sara and backup @vikram.

sara: seeing it, pulling logs now. first guess: autoscaler not keeping up with sudden burst from heavy-embedding job.

maria: has anyone touched pool quotas or been running a big backfill? I see a batch job from customer "mlstudio" hitting embeddings at 2k req/min.

vikram: ack. checking pool metrics: CPU & GPU util at 98%, queue latency increasing. autoscaler max-instances=20, min=4. burst_capacity currently OFF.

sara: immediate mitigation plan: 1) enable burst capacity on dedicated-prod-eu-2, 2) temporarily apply a soft rate limit for embeddings on Hosted (10r/s per-customer) to reduce cross-traffic, 3) throttle mlstudio via per-tenant quota until pool stabilizes.

ken: +1. also consider disabling streaming attachments for embeddings to cut down on KV cache pressure.

sara: executing toggle now — running redwoodctl to enable burst and raise max.

sara: ```
# enabling burst and increasing max instances
redwoodctl pools update --pool dedicated-prod-eu-2 --burst=on --max-instances=40
# verify
redwoodctl pools describe dedicated-prod-eu-2 | grep -E "Burst|MaxInstances"
```

ops-bot: command accepted. API request id=8f9a3b. Operation queued. Estimated scale-up time ~90s.

vikram: while that scales, I’m applying a temporary quota rule for embeddings from Hosted API: per-tenant soft quota 10 req/s with 30s backoff. Will add exception for critical internal jobs.

maria: FYI, I already flagged mlstudio support so they can pause their backfill. pinged them in support channel.

sara: applying rate limit rule via firewall config (traffic-shaper) — one-liner below:

sara: ```
# traffic-shaper pseudo
traffic-shaper set-rate --scope tenant:hosted --model embeddings --rate 10r/s --burst 20
```

oncall-bot: note: applied temporary routing policy to prefer regional fallback model `embedding-compact-v1` for high-volume tenants. This reduces memory pressure.

vikram: scale event in progress. observing instance spin-up logs: "provisioner: attaching GPU instance i-0f..."

ops-bot: autoscaler update: new instances launched=12, current total instances=36. Burst capacity toggled ON.

sara: latency is starting to come down for most customers. Error rate dropped to 3.2% in the last 30s. Good sign.

ken: any downstream impact to Dedicated SLA or cost alerts? Finance will want a note. Also record change in the incident ticket.

maria: documenting: action summary written to INC-2026-4321: enabled burst on dedicated-prod-eu-2, increased max_instances to 40, applied per-tenant soft rate limit for embeddings, switched high-volume tenants to embedding-compact-v1 fallback, notified mlstudio to pause backfill.

sara: setting a guard: will revert burst toggle after 20m stabilization unless we see another surge. Leaving rate limit in place for 1h for safety.

vikram: handoff — I need to step out in 10m. @sara take over post-scale monitoring and customer comms. I will add runbook note: how we enabled burst to avoid repeating the same manual steps.

sara: acknowledged. starting 30m monitor window. adding ephemeral dashboard snapshot to the ticket: `dash/incident-2468200000.png`.

oncall-bot: incident INC-2026-4321 status updated -> mitigated. Severity downgraded to S3.

maria: quick postmortem items: 1) autoscaler config: bump default burst_capacity to ON for dedicated pools handling embeddings by default? 2) add automated burst-policy that triggers when queue latency > 200ms for 60s. 3) improved tenant-level throttling to be auto-applied when pool saturation detected.

sara: creating follow-up ticket PM-ops-784 to track runway changes and automation. putting a note in the release backlog.

ken: thanks team. cc finance and support for customer comms and cost tuning. closing thread after monitoring window.

sara: closing for now — will post final summary when monitor window completes. :white_check_mark:
